items.title: How long packaging takes to arrive
items.question: About how long does each of these take to arrive after we order it?
items.assumption: Today the tool assumes 3–4 weeks for anything we buy, and 8–10 weeks for star foam boxes.

parts.label: MIL-spec clear poly bags — MIL-DTL-117, code BL (not regular commercial bags)
MIL-spec foil moisture-barrier bags (codes BS, SF, SK)
MIL-spec static-shielding bags (code B9)
Weather-resistant boxes (code ED)
Desiccant bags and humidity indicator cards
Star foam boxes (codes NR / NW)
Heat-treated wood: pallets, crates, cable reels

items.title: The label on every bag and box (MIL-STD-129)
items.question: Do our labels look like this sample — with every one of these lines?
items.assumption: Today the tool only says "Mark and label per MIL-STD-129."
details: Every bag (unit pack), inner box and shipping box gets an ID label with these lines, in this order: NSN · CAGE · part number · item description · quantity and unit · contract number · preservation method + date packed · shelf life (if any) · serial numbers (if any).
A 2D bar code (PDF417) holding the NSN (and serial numbers / UIDs), titled "ID DATA". A Code 39 bar code is optional.
If the bag goes inside a box, label BOTH the bag and the box.
All capital letters, at least 0.09 inch tall. Black out old labels on reused boxes.
The shipping box also gets the weight ("WT 14" = 14 lb, rounded up) and a 4×6 Military Shipping Label (MSL) on the same side, right of center.
Method + date: "M31-10/26" means packed by Method 31 in October 2026.
choices: Ours are similar but different (tell us below)
We don't label every bag and box

items.title: DLA rules on every shipment (RP001)
items.question: Do we follow each of these rules on our DLA shipments today?

parts.label: No loose fill — no packing peanuts, crumpled newspaper or shredded paper
No yellow bags, yellow bubble wrap or other yellow packaging
Wood (pallets, crates, cable reels) is heat-treated with the ISPM-15 "bug stamp" showing
Pallets get the label on two sides that touch

items.title: OPI code — are we allowed to substitute?
items.question: Do the OPI codes on our contracts mean this?

parts.label: OPI M — pack exactly as coded: no swapping methods, materials or boxes
OPI O — equal-or-better DoD-approved materials allowed, but the same method, the unit pack no more than 1 inch bigger, and no extra cost
OPI E — only the swaps listed in the contract's special instructions
OPI A — follow the SPI or spec named in the contract

items.title: PACK CODE U — the outside shipping box
items.question: For PACK CODE U, do we use a normal sturdy shipping box — and palletize when more than 25 boxes go to one address?
items.assumption: Today the tool says "Standard commercial box."
details: U = the lowest packing level: any box UPS, FedEx, USPS or a freight carrier will accept, that gets it there undamaged at the lowest rate.
Hazardous material still follows DOT shipping rules.
If one shipment has more than 25 boxes of 1.5 cubic feet or less (no side over 40 inches), they must go on a pallet, a box pallet or in a container.
choices: Yes — regular box, and a pallet over 25 boxes
Regular box, but we never palletize
We use a specific box — tell us which

items.title: INTRMDTE CONT QTY: AAA — how many per inner box
items.question: When INTRMDTE CONT QTY says AAA, how do you decide how many bags go in each inner box?
items.assumption: Today the tool says "You choose how many per box," within these limits.
details: No more than 100 unit packs per box.
No more than 40 lb.
No more than 1.5 cubic feet, with at least two sides 16 inches or less.
Odd or short counts go in the smallest box that fits.
Unit packs over 10 lb or 0.375 cubic feet don't get an inner box at all.
Example: 250 small bags → 100 + 100 + 50 in three boxes.
choices: As many as fit, up to 100 bags / 40 lb / 1.5 cu ft
All the bags in one box, whatever the count
Whatever box we have on the shelf decides it

items.title: CUSH/DUNN THKNESS — where the thickness goes
items.question: When CUSH/DUNN THKNESS says C (3/4 inch), where does that 3/4 inch of cushioning go?
items.assumption: Today the tool says "at least 3/4 inch thick on every side that needs protection; cover every sharp edge."
details: A = 1/4 in · B = 1/2 in · C = 3/4 in · D = 1 in · F = 1-1/2 in · H = 2 in
The box must then be sized: item size + 2 × cushion thickness in each direction.
choices: All six sides of the item
Only the sides that need protection
Just around sharp edges and projections

items.title: CUSH/DUNN MAT: NA — the cushioning
items.question: When CUSH/DUNN MAT says NA, what do we actually wrap the part in?
items.assumption: Today the tool says "Bubble wrap or foam." NA is a real code — it does not mean "not applicable".
details: NA allows: bubble wrap (PPP-C-795), open-cell foam (A-A-3129) or polyethylene foam.
It must not be yellow, and no loose fill.
Static-sensitive parts need the pink anti-static versions instead (codes LT, NB).

items.title: PRES MTHD 10 — no barrier bag
items.question: For PRES MTHD 10, do we ship the part with no bag — just cushioned so it can't move in its box?
items.assumption: Today the tool says "No bag — just protect it."
details: Method 10 = physical protection only: clean and dry, no oil, cushion / block / brace so it can't move.
No leak test and no seal test.
BUT if the UNIT CONT code is a bag (e.g. A1 or BL), the bag is still required.
choices: Yes, no bag unless UNIT CONT names one

items.title: MIL-spec bags vs. regular commercial bags (Uline)
items.question: For each of these contract callouts: do we need a real MIL-spec bag, or is a regular commercial bag OK?
items.assumption: The tool's reading of the standard: BL, A1 and Methods 31 / 32 need a real MIL-DTL-117 bag. A2, commercial-packaging (ASTM D3951) contracts and Method 10 with no bag named can use a regular commercial bag.
details: BL = MIL-DTL-117 Type III, Class B, Style 2: a clear, waterproof, heat-sealable bag made from A-A-3174 or MIL-PRF-22191 Type III film. Its seals must pass a 50 oz strength test.
A regular commercial poly bag isn't made or certified to MIL-DTL-117, so it doesn't meet a BL callout — even if it looks the same.
When buying MIL-spec bags, ask the supplier for a certificate of conformance to MIL-DTL-117 Type III, Class B, Style 2.
OPI O ("equal or better") does not make a commercial bag OK: substitutes must be DoD-approved materials.

parts.label: UNIT CONT: BL, or PRES MTHD 31 / 32
UNIT CONT: A1 — "any bag authorized by MIL-DTL-117", taped or stapled
UNIT CONT: A2 — "any bag or sack used by the vendor"
Commercial-packaging contracts ("commercially packaged per ASTM D3951")
PRES MTHD 10 with no bag named in UNIT CONT

items.title: PRES MTHD 31 — clear bag, heat sealed
items.question: For PRES MTHD 31, do we seal the MIL-spec clear bag like this — and do we do the seal tests?
details: Bag: a MIL-spec clear poly bag (MIL-DTL-117 Type III, Class B, Style 2 — code BL), not a regular commercial bag.
Cushion sharp edges first so nothing punches through the bag.
Squeeze out the air, then heat-seal — one continuous seal.
The standard requires a leak test and a seal-strength test on samples (a 1-inch strip of the seal must hold 50 oz for 5 minutes).
If the contract adds a box, the cushioning goes between the bag and the box.
choices: Yes, but we don't do the tests
We seal differently — tell us how

items.title: Commercial packaging contracts (ASTM D3951)
items.question: On ASTM D3951 commercial-packaging contracts, do we pack the same as a normal commercial order — plus these DLA rules?
details: These contracts have no packaging codes — just "commercially packaged per ASTM D3951".
DLA rules still apply: no loose fill, no yellow material, heat-treated wood, MIL-STD-129 labels.
If the item is hazardous, it must be packed per DLA rule IP025 instead.
choices: Yes, same as commercial (plus the DLA rules)
We still do some MIL-style steps — tell us which

items.title: Bag codes in the UNIT CONT box
items.question: When UNIT CONT names a bag code (BL, BS, B9…), do we ever use a different bag than the one named?
items.assumption: The tool lists exactly the bag in the code and flags it YELLOW (buy).
details: BL = clear poly bag · BS = foil moisture-barrier bag · SE = clear moisture-barrier bag · B9 = static-shielding bag · BE / BV = opaque greaseproof bag · A1 = any MIL-spec bag, taped or stapled shut
With OPI M, no substitutions are allowed. With OPI O, an equal-or-better bag is allowed.

items.title: PRES MTHD 32 / 42 — box inside the bag
items.question: For PRES MTHD 32 and 42 (box inside the bag), do we pack it like this?
details: Method 32: item in a snug inner box → into a clear poly bag (BL) → heat seal.
Method 42: inner box → foil bag → heat seal → weather-resistant outer box.
Inner box corners must be blunted (folded or taped over) — inspectors check this.
Label both the bag and the outer box.
choices: Yes, but we don't blunt the corners
We do it differently — tell us how

items.title: PACK CODE Q — shipping box from the table
items.question: For PACK CODE Q at PACKING LEVEL B, what shipping box do we use?
items.assumption: The tool says: "Box from the table for the level," and for Level B tells purchasing to buy a weather-resistant shipping box.
details: Q = choose the shipping container from MIL-STD-2073 Table C-II for the packing level printed on the contract.
Level A = toughest (overseas, outdoor storage). Level B = weather-resistant domestic shipping.
choices: Depends on the item — tell us

items.title: Box count written in the special instructions
items.question: When INTRMDTE CONT QTY says AAA but the special instructions say "ICQ = 008", do we put exactly 8 bags in each box?
items.assumption: The tool uses the number from the instructions and shows a warning that it overrode the code.
details: ICQ = intermediate container quantity = how many bags go in each inner box.

items.title: MIL-PRF-23199 contracts
items.question: For MIL-PRF-23199 items (NSN 6150-01-022-6004), do we pack them like this?
details: Clean and dry. Cap every opening with brightly colored caps.
Seal each item in a green 0.006-inch poly envelope, heat-sealed.
ID label inside the envelope, NSN bar code label outside.
Box it: one packing list inside, two outside.
Keep our written packaging procedure on file for the Government.

items.title: Star foam boxes (NR / NW)
items.question: Are UNIT CONT NR and NW what you call "star packaging" — a reusable box with star-shaped foam inserts?
items.assumption: The tool flags NR and NW RED: 8–10 weeks, very expensive.
details: NR = reusable box with vertical star foam inserts (PPP-B-1672 Type I).
NW = reusable box with horizontal star foam inserts (PPP-B-1672 Type IV).

items.title: UNIT CONT: ZZ — "BAG BL WITHIN BOX ED"
items.question: Does "BAG BL WITHIN BOX ED" mean: the part goes in a BL bag, then the bag goes in an ED box?
items.assumption: The tool lists both containers but doesn't yet say which goes inside which.
choices: Yes — part in bag, bag in box
items.textMatch: BAG BL WITHIN BOX|IN BAG BL

items.title: PRESV MAT 49 — our own oil or grease
items.question: When PRESV MAT says 49 ("vendor's protective grease or oil"), what do we put on the part — and what wraps it?
items.assumption: The tool says: "Our normal oil or grease coating," and warns that anything touching the oiled surface must be greaseproof.
details: Any wrap touching an oiled surface must be greaseproof barrier paper (MIL-PRF-121) or aluminum foil.

items.title: Reusable foam boxes (NS / NV)
items.question: Are UNIT CONT NS and NV (reusable foam boxes) as slow and expensive as star packaging?
items.assumption: The tool flags them RED, same as star packaging. Not on any of our contracts yet.
details: NS = reusable box with folding foam inserts (PPP-B-1672 Type II).
NV = reusable box with telescoping foam inserts (PPP-B-1672 Type III).

items.title: Desiccant packs (Methods 50–55)
items.question: For PRES MTHD 50–55 (desiccant packs): do we keep each of these on the shelf, or buy it per job?
items.assumption: The tool flags desiccant methods YELLOW (buy, 3–4 weeks). Not on any of our contracts yet.

parts.label: Desiccant bags (MIL-D-3464)
Humidity indicator cards (MS20003)
Foil moisture-barrier bags

items.title: PRES MTHD 51–53 — desiccant pack steps
items.question: For PRES MTHD 51–53, is this the right order for packing with desiccant?
details: 1. Use a bag about 5 inches bigger than normal — enough to reseal it twice after inspection.
2. Put the humidity indicator card where it can be read (behind the window, or just inside the seal).
3. Open the desiccant LAST, right before sealing. It must not touch the part or carry any weight.
4. Squeeze out the air and heat-seal. Leak test and seal test.
5. One item per pack. Mark the box "PACKAGED WITH DESICCANT".

items.title: A sealed bag with no box named
items.question: If a part is just in a sealed bag and the contract names no inner box, do we still put the bag in a box before the shipping carton?
items.assumption: The tool warns: "Bagged unit packs normally go in an intermediate box. The contract governs."
choices: No — the bag goes straight in the shipping box

items.title: Common mistakes
items.question: How often does each of these mistakes happen when packing DLA orders?

parts.label: A regular commercial bag used where a MIL-spec bag was required
Heat seal not continuous, or bag not sealed at all
Missing or wrong MIL-STD-129 label (bag or box)
Wrong number of bags per inner box
Sharp edges not cushioned — bag or box punctured
Packing peanuts, newspaper or yellow material used
Wood pallet or crate without the ISPM-15 heat-treat stamp
Weather-resistant box needed but a regular box used
Packing to how we did it last time instead of the current contract

details: Use "+ Add a note" for any other mistake we should warn about, or anything the depot has rejected.
